D.treatment: children with no apparent mathematical difficulties
D.comparison: children with dyslexia and mathematical difficulties

cells.quote:
In the WJ-IV Calculation test, around 30% of children with no apparent difﬁculties in mathematics (8 out of 25 children) obtained a result below the 16 percentiles outside the average range (any score that falls one standard deviation below the mean indicates below-average performance). However, not one of these children obtained a low score in prior mathematical assessments using the WJ-IV (Broad Math, Applied Problems, Fluency), Wechsler Individual Achievement Test (WIAT; Math, Numerical, Problem Solving, Fluency), Kaufman Test of Educational Achievement (KTEA; Math Concepts and Applications, Computation, Fluency, Problem Solving), or the Feifer Assessment of Mathematics83. Furthermore, their previous and current history did not indicate any symptoms of mathematical difﬁculty.

On the other hand, ~25% of the children with dyslexia and mathematics difﬁculties (12 out of 47) obtained a score on the WJ-IV Calculation test at or greater than the 25th percentile (average performance); of these children, none had deﬁcits in number processing, ﬁve had deﬁcits on arithmetic facts retrieval, three on arithmetical procedures, and four on geometrical abilities.
cells.note: The study reports discrepant WJ-IV Calculation classifications across clinically defined groups, but does not report a direct statistical comparison or an effect size.

cells.quote: The other 50 participants from our dyslexic cohort (50/75, 66.6%), classified by the clinicians’ team as having deficits in mathematics, performed poorly on specific subtests of the MCB corresponding to their specific deficit (refer to Fig. 1b).
cells.note: The study reports poorer performance in the mathematical-deficit groups, with the weakness varying by mathematical domain.

cells.quote: In the WJ-IV Calculation test, around 30% of children with no apparent difficulties in mathematics (8 out of 25 children) obtained a result below the 16 percentiles outside the average range (any score that falls one standard deviation below the mean indicates below-average performance).
cells.note: This indicates false-positive low scores among children classified as having no mathematical difficulties.

cells.quote: On the other hand, ~25% of the children with dyslexia and mathematics difficulties (12 out of 47) obtained a score on the WJ-IV Calculation test at or greater than the 25th percentile (average performance); of these children, none had deficits in number processing, five had deficits on arithmetic facts retrieval, three on arithmetical procedures, and four on geometrical abilities.
cells.note: This indicates that the WJ-IV Calculation test can yield average performance for children classified as having mathematical difficulties, particularly for non-number deficit profiles.

cells.quote: Children with deﬁcits in number processing (n = 10, 13.3% of dyslexia sample) performed signiﬁcantly lower than all other groups on number subtests and obtained low scores in most of the MCB’s subtests.
cells.note: The study used domain-specific MCB performance to distinguish mathematical-deficit profiles; this contrasts with the weaker capture of non-number deficits by commonly administered assessments.
